verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列全会众说：你们要圣洁，因为我耶和华―你们的　神是圣洁的。
verses.en: “Speak to the whole congregation of the Israelites and tell them, ‘You must be holy because I, the Lord your God, am holy.

verses.zh: 你们各人都当孝敬父母，也要守我的安息日。我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: Each of you must respect his mother and his father,[NOTE:1] and you must keep my Sabbaths. I am the Lord your God.
notes: Heb “A man his mother and his father you [plural] shall fear.” The LXX, Syriac, Vulgate, and certain Targum mss reverse the order, “his father and his mother.” The term “fear” is subject to misunderstanding by the modern reader, so “respect” has been used in the translation. Cf. NAB, NRSV “revere”; NASB “reverence.”

verses.zh: 你们不可偏向虚无的神，也不可为自己铸造神像。我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: Do not turn to idols,[NOTE:1] and you must not make for yourselves gods of cast metal. I am the Lord your God.
notes: Regarding the difficult etymology and meaning of the term for “idols” (אֱלִילִים, ʾelilim), see B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 126; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 304; N. H. Snaith, Leviticus and Numbers (NBC), 89; and Judith M. Hadley, NIDOTTE 1:411. It appears to be a diminutive play on words with אֵל (ʾel, “god; God”) and, perhaps at the same time, recalls a common Semitic word for “worthless; weak; powerless; nothingness.” Snaith suggests a rendering of “worthless godlings.”

verses.zh: 「你们献平安祭给耶和华的时候，要献得可蒙悦纳。
verses.en: “‘When you sacrifice a peace-offering sacrifice to the Lord, you must sacrifice it so that it is accepted for you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for your acceptance”; cf. NIV, NLT “it will be accepted on your behalf.”

verses.zh: 这祭物要在献的那一天和第二天吃，若有剩到第三天的，就必用火焚烧。
verses.en: It must be eaten on the day of your sacrifice and on the following day,[NOTE:1] but what is left over until the third day must be burned up.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from the following day” (HALOT 572 s.v. מָחֳרָת 2.b).
Heb “shall be burned with fire”; KJV “shall be burnt in the fire.” Because “to burn with fire” is redundant in contemporary English the present translation simply has “must be burned up.”

verses.zh: 第三天若再吃，这就为可憎恶的，必不蒙悦纳。
verses.en: If, however, it is eaten[NOTE:1] on the third day, it is spoiled;[NOTE:2] it will not be accepted,
notes: Heb “And if being eaten [infinitive absolute] it is eaten [finite verb].” For the infinitive absolute used to highlight contrast rather than emphasis see GKC 343 §113.p.
Or “desecrated,” or “defiled,” or “forbidden.” For this difficult term see J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:422, on Lev 7:18.

verses.zh: 凡吃的人必担当他的罪孽；因为他亵渎了耶和华的圣物，那人必从民中剪除。
verses.en: and the one who eats it will bear his punishment for iniquity[NOTE:1] because he has profaned[NOTE:2] what is holy to the Lord.[NOTE:3] That person will be cut off from his people.[NOTE:4]
notes: See the note on Lev 17:16 above.
Regarding “profaned,” see the note on Lev 10:10 above.
Heb “the holiness of the Lord.”
On the “cut off” penalty see the note on Lev 7:20.

verses.zh: 「在你们的地收割庄稼，不可割尽田角，也不可拾取所遗落的。
verses.en: “‘When you gather in the harvest[NOTE:1] of your land, you must not completely harvest the corner of your field,[NOTE:2] and you must not gather up the gleanings of your harvest.
notes: Heb “And in your harvesting the harvest.”
Heb “you shall not complete the corner of your field to harvest.”

verses.zh: 不可摘尽葡萄园的果子，也不可拾取葡萄园所掉的果子；要留给穷人和寄居的。我是耶和华你―们的　神。
verses.en: You must not pick your vineyard bare,[NOTE:1] and you must not gather up the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You must leave them for the poor and the resident foreigner.[NOTE:2] I am the Lord your God.
notes: Heb “And you shall not deal severely with your vineyard.”
On the Hebrew ger (גֵּר) “resident foreigner” see notes at Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:11. On the privilege of gleaning see also Lev 23:22; Deut 14:29; 24:19-21.

verses.zh: 「你们不可偷盗，不可欺骗，也不可彼此说谎。
verses.en: “‘You must not steal, you must not tell lies, and you must not deal falsely with your fellow citizen.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you shall not deal falsely a man with his fellow citizen.”

verses.zh: 不可指着我的名起假誓，亵渎你　神的名。我是耶和华。
verses.en: You must not swear falsely[NOTE:1] in my name, so that you do not profane[NOTE:2] the name of your God. I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “And you shall not swear to the falsehood.”
Heb “and you shall not profane”; NAB “thus profaning.”

verses.zh: 「不可欺压你的邻舍，也不可抢夺他的物。雇工人的工价，不可在你那里过夜，留到早晨。
verses.en: You must not oppress your neighbor or commit robbery against your neighbor.[NOTE:1] You must not withhold[NOTE:2] the wages of the hired laborer overnight until morning.
notes: Heb “You shall not oppress your neighbor and you shall not rob.”
Heb “hold back with you”; perhaps “hold back for yourself” (cf. NRSV “keep for yourself”).

verses.zh: 不可咒骂聋子，也不可将绊脚石放在瞎子面前，只要敬畏你的　神。我是耶和华。
verses.en: You must not curse a deaf person or put a stumbling block in front of a blind person.[NOTE:1] You must fear[NOTE:2] your God; I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “You shall not curse a deaf [person] and before a blind [person] you shall not put a stumbling block.”
Heb “And you shall fear.” Many English versions (e.g., KJV, ASV, NAB, NASB, NIV) regard the Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) as adversative in force here (“but”).

verses.zh: 「你们施行审判，不可行不义；不可偏护穷人，也不可重看有势力的人，只要按着公义审判你的邻舍。
verses.en: “‘You[NOTE:1] must not deal unjustly in judgment:[NOTE:2] You must neither show partiality to the poor nor honor the rich.[NOTE:3] You must judge your fellow citizen fairly.[NOTE:4]
notes: Smr has the singular rather than the plural “you” of the MT, which brings this verb form into line with the ones surrounding it.
Heb “You shall not do injustice in judgment” (NASB similar); cf. NIV “do not pervert justice.”
Heb “You shall not lift up faces of poor [people] and you shall not honor faces of great.”
Heb “In righteousness you shall judge your fellow citizen.”

verses.zh: 不可在民中往来搬弄是非，也不可与邻舍为敌，置之于死（原文是流他的血）。我是耶和华。
verses.en: You must not go about as a slanderer among your people.[NOTE:1] You must not stand idly by when your neighbor’s life is at stake.[NOTE:2] I am the Lord.
notes: The term רָכִיל (rakhil) is traditionally rendered “slanderer” here (so NASB, NIV, NRSV; see also J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 304, 316), but the exact meaning is uncertain (see the discussion in B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 129). It is sometimes related to I רָכַל (rakhal, “to go about as a trader [or “merchant”]”; BDB 940 s.v. רָכַל), and taken to refer to cutthroat business dealings, but there may be a II רָכַל, the meaning of which is dubious (HALOT 1237 s.v. II *רכל). Some would render it “to go about as a spy.”

Heb “You shall not stand on the blood of your neighbor.” This part of the verse is also difficult to interpret. The rendering here suggests that one will not allow a neighbor to be victimized, whether in court (cf. v. 15) or in any other situation (see the discussion in B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 129).

verses.zh: 「不可心里恨你的弟兄；总要指摘你的邻舍，免得因他担罪。
verses.en: You must not hate your brother in your heart. You must surely reprove your fellow citizen so that you do not incur sin on account of him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and you will not lift up on him sin.” The meaning of the line is somewhat obscure. It means either (1) that one should rebuke one’s neighbor when he sins lest one also becomes guilty, which is the way it is rendered here (see NIV, NRSV, NEB, JB; see also B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 129-30, and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 303, and the discussion on pp. 316-17), or (2) one may rebuke one’s neighbor without incurring sin just as long as he does not hate him in his heart (see the first part of the verse; cf. NASB, NAB).

verses.zh: 不可报仇，也不可埋怨你本国的子民，却要爱人如己。我是耶和华。
verses.en: You must not take vengeance or bear a grudge against[NOTE:1] any of your people,[NOTE:2] but you must love your neighbor as yourself.[NOTE:3] I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “and you shall not retain [anger?].” This line seems to refer to the retaining or maintaining of some vengeful feelings toward someone. Compare the combination of the same terms for taking vengeance and maintaining wrath against enemies in Nahum 1:2 (see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 305).
Heb “the sons of your people.”

Some scholars make a distinction between the verb אָהֵב (ʾahev, “to love”) with the direct object and the more unusual construction with the preposition ל (lamed) as it is here and in Lev 19:34 and 2 Chr 19:2 only. If there is a distinction, the construction here probably calls for direct and helpful action toward one’s neighbor (see the discussion in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 305, and esp. 317-18). Such love stands in contrast to taking vengeance or bearing a grudge against someone and, in NT terms, amounts to fulfilling the so-called “golden rule” (Matt 7:12).

verses.zh: 「你们要守我的律例。不可叫你的牲畜与异类配合；不可用两样搀杂的种种你的地，也不可用两样搀杂的料做衣服穿在身上。
verses.en: You must keep my statutes. You must not allow two different kinds of your animals to breed together,[NOTE:1] you must not sow your field with two different kinds of seed, and you must not wear[NOTE:2] a garment made of two different kinds of material.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Your animals, you shall not cross-breed two different kinds.”
Heb “you shall not cause to go up on you.”
Cf. Deut 22:11 where the Hebrew term translated “two different kinds” (כִּלְאַיִם, kilʾayim) refers to a mixture of linen and wool woven together in a garment.

verses.zh: 「婢女许配了丈夫，还没有被赎、得释放，人若与她行淫，二人要受刑罚，却不把他们治死，因为婢女还没有得自由。
verses.en: “‘When a man goes to bed with a woman for intercourse,[NOTE:1] although she is a slave woman designated for another man and she has not yet been ransomed, or freedom has not been granted to her, there will be an obligation to pay compensation.[NOTE:2] They must not be put to death, because she was not free.
notes: Heb “And a man when he lies with a woman, the lying of seed.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakav) “to lie down” acts as a euphemism, implying going to bed for sexual relations. In this case, the phrase “lying for (a man’s) seed” specifies that it refers to sexual intercourse.

That is, the woman had previously been assigned for marriage to another man but the marriage deal had not yet been consummated. In the meantime, the woman has lost her virginity and has, therefore, lost part of her value to the master in the sale to the man for whom she had been designated. Compensation was, therefore, required (see the explanation in B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 130-31).

verses.zh: 那人要把赎愆祭，就是一只公绵羊牵到会幕门口、耶和华面前。
verses.en: He must bring his guilt offering to the Lord at the entrance of the Meeting Tent, a guilt-offering ram,[NOTE:1]
notes: On the guilt offering see the note on Lev 5:15 above.

verses.zh: 祭司要用赎愆祭的羊在耶和华面前赎他所犯的罪，他的罪就必蒙赦免。
verses.en: and the priest is to make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before the Lord for his sin that he has committed,[NOTE:1] and he will be forgiven[NOTE:2] of his sin[NOTE:3] that he has committed.
notes: Heb “on his sin which he has sinned.”
Heb “there shall be forgiveness to him” or “it shall be forgiven to him.”
Heb “from his sin.”

verses.zh: 「你们到了迦南地，栽种各样结果子的树木，就要以所结的果子如未受割礼的一样。三年之久，你们要以这些果子，如未受割礼的，是不可吃的。
verses.en: “‘When you enter the land and plant any fruit tree,[NOTE:1] you must consider its fruit to be forbidden.[NOTE:2] Three years it will be forbidden to you;[NOTE:3] it must not be eaten.
notes: Heb “tree of food”; KJV, ASV, NASB, NRSV “trees for food.”

Heb “you shall circumcise its fruit [as] its foreskin,” taking the fruit to be that which is to be removed and, therefore, forbidden. Since the fruit is uncircumcised it is forbidden (see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 306, and esp. B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 131-32).
Heb “it shall be to you uncircumcised.”

verses.zh: 但第四年所结的果子全要成为圣，用以赞美耶和华。
verses.en: In the fourth year all its fruit will be holy, praise offerings[NOTE:1] to the Lord.
notes: See B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 132, where the translation reads “set aside for jubilation”; a special celebration before the Lord.

verses.zh: 第五年，你们要吃那树上的果子，好叫树给你们结果子更多。我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: Then in the fifth year you may eat its fruit to add its produce to your harvest.[NOTE:1] I am the Lord your God.
notes: Heb “to add to you its produce.” The rendering here assumes that the point of this clause is simply that finally being allowed to eat the fruit in the fifth year adds the fruit of the tree to their harvest. Some take the verb to be from אָסַף (ʾasaf, “to gather”) rather than יָסַף (yasaf, “to add; to increase”), rendering the verse, “to gather to you the produce” (E. S. Gerstenberger, Leviticus [OTL], 260, and see the versions referenced in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 306). Others take it to mean that by following the regulations given previously they will honor the Lord so that the Lord will cause the trees to increase the amount of fruit they would normally produce (Hartley, 303, 306; cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).

verses.zh: 「你们不可吃带血的物；不可用法术，也不可观兆。
verses.en: “‘You must not eat anything with the blood still in it.[NOTE:1] You must not practice either divination or soothsaying.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “You shall not eat on the blood.” See the extensive remarks in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 319-20, and B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 132-33. The LXX has “on the mountains,” suggesting that this is a prohibition against illegitimate places and occasions of worship, not the eating of blood.

Heb “You shall not practice divination and you shall not practice soothsaying”; cf. NRSV “practice augury or witchcraft.” For suggestions regarding the practices involved see B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 133, and J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 320.

verses.zh: 头的周围（或译：两鬓）不可剃，胡须的周围也不可损坏。
verses.en: You must not round off the corners of the hair on your head or ruin the corners of your beard.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and you [singular] shall not ruin the corner of your [singular] beard.” Smr, LXX, Syriac, and Tg. Ps.-J. have the plural pronouns (i.e., “you” and “your” plural) rather than the singular of the MT.

verses.zh: 不可为死人用刀划身，也不可在身上刺花纹。我是耶和华。
verses.en: You must not slash your body for a dead person[NOTE:1] or incise a tattoo on yourself.[NOTE:2] I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “And slash for the soul you shall not give.” The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “soul, person, life”) can sometimes refer to a “dead person” (cf. Lev 21:1, 5; 22:5). See J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 306, 320-21.
Heb “and a writing of incision you shall not give in you.”

verses.zh: 「不可辱没你的女儿，使她为娼妓，恐怕地上的人专向淫乱，地就满了大恶。
verses.en: Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute,[NOTE:1] so that the land does not practice prostitution and become full of lewdness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to make her practice harlotry.” Some recent English versions regard this as religious or temple prostitution (cf. TEV, CEV).
Heb “and the land become full of lewdness.” Regarding the term “lewdness,” see the note on Lev 18:17 above.

verses.zh: 你们要守我的安息日，敬我的圣所。我是耶和华。
verses.en: “‘You must keep my Sabbaths and fear my sanctuary. I am the Lord.

verses.zh: 「不可偏向那些交鬼的和行巫术的；不可求问他们，以致被他们玷污了。我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: Do not turn to the spirits of the dead and do not seek familiar spirits[NOTE:1] to become unclean by them. I am the Lord your God.
notes: The prohibition here concerns those who would seek special knowledge through the spirits of the dead, whether the dead in general or dead relatives in particular (i.e., familiar spirits; see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 321, and B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 134). Cf. Lev 20:6 below.

verses.zh: 「在白发的人面前，你要站起来；也要尊敬老人，又要敬畏你的　神。我是耶和华。
verses.en: You must stand up in the presence of the aged, honor the presence of an elder, and fear your God. I am the Lord.

verses.zh: 「若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。
verses.en: When a resident foreigner[NOTE:1] lives with you in your land, you must not oppress him.
notes: The noun “foreigner” (גֵּר; ger) is based on the same verbal root as “lives” (גּוּר; gur), which means “to sojourn, to dwell as an alien.” On the Hebrew ger (גֵּר) “resident foreigner” see notes at Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:11. On not oppressing the ger, see also Exod 22:21; Deut 24:14, 17; 27:19.

verses.zh: 和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。我是耶和华―你们的　神。
verses.en: The resident foreigner[NOTE:1] who lives with you must be to you as a native citizen among you; so[NOTE:2] you must love the foreigner as yourself, because you were foreigners[NOTE:3] in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
notes: The noun “foreigner” (גֵּר; ger) is based on the same verbal root as “lives” (גּוּר; gur), which means “to sojourn, to dwell as an alien.”
Heb “and.” The Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) can be considered to have resultative force here.

The same term ger (גֵּר) is used for the resident foreigner living in Israel and of the Israelite who lived in Israel, despite the very different social conditions of each. A foreign resident has differing status in different countries. The Israelites were slaves in Egypt, but the resident foreigner in Israel was under the same laws (civil and religious) as the Israelite and could worship the Lord as part of the covenant community. Several passages emphasize equal standing under Mosaic Law (Exod 12:49; Lev 24:22; Num 9:14; 15:15, 16, 26, 29; 19:10; 35:15; Deut 1:16) or similar obligations (Exod 20:10; 23:12; Lev 16:29; 17:10, 12, 13; 18:26; 24:16; Num 15:14). For more on the ger (גֵּר), see the notes at Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:11.

verses.zh: 「你们施行审判，不可行不义；在尺、秤、升、斗上也是如此。
verses.en: You must not do injustice in the regulation of measures, whether of length, weight, or volume.[NOTE:1]
notes: That is, liquid capacity (HALOT 640 s.v. מְשׂוּרָה). Cf. ASV, NIV, NRSV, TEV “quantity”; NAB, NASB “capacity.”

verses.zh: 要用公道天平、公道法码、公道升斗、公道秤。我是耶和华―你们的　神，曾把你们从埃及地领出来的。
verses.en: You must have honest balances,[NOTE:1] honest weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin.[NOTE:2] I am the Lord your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt.
notes: Heb “balances of righteousness,” and so throughout this sentence.
An ephah is a dry measure which measures about four gallons, or perhaps one third of a bushel, while a hin is a liquid measure of about 3.6 liters (= approximately 1 gallon).

verses.zh: 你们要谨守遵行我一切的律例典章。我是耶和华。」
verses.en: You must be sure to obey all my statutes and regulations.[NOTE:1] I am the Lord.’”
notes: Heb “And you shall keep all my statutes and all my regulations and you shall do them.” This appears to be a kind of verbal hendiadys, where the first verb is a modifier of the action of the second verb (see GKC 386 §120.d, although שָׁמַר [shamar, “to keep”] is not cited there; cf. Lev 22:31).

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must
not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter deals with various regulations (note the curses of Deuteronomy 27). These are repeated in several places
in the Pentateuch. This shows some type of editing. Remember, OT compilations or editing are also inspired.

- List of subject and parallels.

- be holy for I am holy, Lev. 19:2 ‒ Exod. 19:5-6; Lev. 11:44-45; 19:2; 20:7,26; Num. 15:40; Deut. 7:6; 14:2,21

- honor parents, Lev. 19:3 ‒ Exod. 20:12; Deut. 5:16; 27:16 (see full note online at Deut. 5:16)

- keep the sabbath, Lev. 19:3b ‒ Exod. 20:8; 23:12; 31:15; Lev. 19:30; Deut. 5:12-14

- no idolatry, Lev. 19:4 ‒ Exod. 20:3-4,23; 34:17; Deut. 4:15-19; 5:7-9

- peace offering regulations, Lev. 19:5-8 ‒ Leviticus 3; 7:28-34

- gleaning (see full note online at Deut. 24:19-23), Lev. 19:9-10 ‒ Lev. 23:22; Deut. 23:24-25; 24:19-21

- no stealing, Lev. 19:11 ‒ Exod. 20:15; 21:16; Deut. 5:19 (may refer to kidnaping, see Deut. 24:7)

- no false witness, Lev. 19:11 ‒ Exod. 20:16; Deut. 5:20 (see full note online at Deut. 5:20)

- do not take YHWH's name in vain, Lev. 19:12 ‒ Exod. 20:7; Deut. 5:11; 6:13; 10:20 (see full note online at Deut. 5:11)

- do not oppress or rob neighbor, Lev. 19:13a ‒ Exod. 22:7-15,21-23

- pay the hired help immediately, Lev. 19:13b ‒ Deut. 24:14-15

- treat the disabled with care, not malice, Lev. 19:14 ‒ Deut. 27:18

- be fair in judgment, Lev. 19:15-16 ‒ Lev. 23:3,6-9; Deut. 1:17; 16:19; 24:17; 27:19,25 (see full note online at Deut. 1:17)

- do not hate or take revenge on your covenant partner but love him, Lev. 19:17-18 ‒ Deut. 32:35 (see full note online)

- do not mix things, Lev. 19:19 ‒ Deut. 22:9-11

- improper sexual activity with a slave, Lev. 19:20-22 ‒ Deut. 22:23-27

- initial dedication of fruit tree harvest to God until the fifth year, Lev. 19:23-25

- do not eat blood, Lev. 19:26a ‒ Lev. 3:17; 7:26-27; Deut. 12:16,23-25

- do not practice divination or soothsaying, Lev. 19:26b,31 ‒ Lev. 20:6; 27; Deut. 18:9-13,14 (see full note online at Deut. 18:9-14)

- do not cut your beards, Lev. 19:27-28 ‒ Lev. 21:5; Deut. 14:1 (see full note online)

- do not sell/give your daughter to prostitution, Lev. 19:29 ‒ Deut. 23:17-18; for priest's daughters see Lev. 21:9
(see full note online at Deut. 23:17-18)

- revere YHWH's sanctuary, Lev. 19:30b ‒ Lev. 26:2

- honor the aged, Lev. 19:32

- treat the stranger/sojourner well, Lev. 19:33-34 ‒ Exod. 22:21

- fair commerce, Lev. 19:35-36 ‒ Deut. 25:13-16

- Notice how Israel made no distinction between what we now label as "cultic" and "moral." All of life was sacred and a
gift from God. Not only the Sabbath but every day, the people of God model His character to a pagan world.

- There is a lot of confusion in this chapter between SINGULAR and PLURAL in the MT
and the ancient versions.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 19:1

1Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 19:2-4

2"Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel and say to them, 'You shall be holy, for I the
Lord your God am holy. 3Every one of you shall reverence his mother
and his father, and you shall keep My sabbaths; I am the Lord your God. 4Do
not turn to idols or make for yourselves molten gods; I am the Lord your God.'"

19:2 "Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel" This is a Piel IMPERATIVE,
like so many in the chapters in Leviticus, but this one is uniquely addressed to the whole congregation (cf. Exod. 12:3).

▣ "You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy" The VERB
(BDB 224, KB 243, Qal IMPERFECT) is used as an IMPERATIVE or
JUSSIVE, with an emphasis on "continue to be holy," as are all the VERBS in Lev. 19:2b-5).
This is the reason for all of these stipulations. God is to be reflected in the daily life of His people (cf. Lev. 1:44,45; 20:7,26;
Matt. 5:48). See SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY and
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE.

19:3 "you shall reverence his mother and his father" Notice that a stable family pattern, reflected in Exod. 20:12,
is what will make a strong society. There are several texts that express this same truth from a negative perspective
(cf. Exod. 21:15,17; Lev. 20:9; Deut. 21:18-21; Pro. 20:20; 23:22; 30:17).

Also notice that the mother is mentioned first (cf. Lev. 21:2), which shows the respect for her in the
Hebrew society. The LXX, Peshitta, and Vulgate reverse the order of the MT.

The VERB "revere" (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal PERFECT) is
literally "fear." It is used in several senses.

- fear

- of God ‒ Gen. 3:10; 18:15; 20:8; 28:12

- of men ‒ Gen. 32:8; 42:3; 43:18; Exod. 2:14; 14:10; Deut. 20:8; 31:8

- in awe

- of God ‒ Exod. 9:30; Lev. 19:14,32; 25:17,36,43

- of men ‒ Exod. 34:30 (i.e., Moses)

- honor/respect/fear

- God ‒ Gen. 42:18; Exod. 1:17,21; 18:21; Deut. 4:10; 6:2,13,24; 8:6; 10:12,20; 14:23; 17:19; 31:12-13

- parents ‒ Lev. 19:3 (Deut. 5:16, different VERB)

- YHWH's sanctuary ‒ Lev. 19:30; 26:2

- leaders (i.e., Moses and Joshua) ‒ Josh. 4:14

- not fear other gods ‒ Jdgs. 6:10

▣ "you shall keep My sabbaths" The VERB, like all VERBS in
Lev. 19:2b-5, is IMPERFECT, which denotes continual action. Notice "sabbath" is PLURAL.
This admonition means "keep all the regulations about My sabbath worship, week by week and year by year. It is
important to Him (cf. Gen. 2:1-3; Exod. 20:8-11).

19:4 "Do not turn to idols" The term translated "idols" is difficult to define (BDB 47, KB 55).

- diminutive of El (the general name for god in the ANE; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A)

- from Arabic root ‒ useless

- from Akkadian root ‒ powerless

- NET Bible suggests "worthless," p. 254 and mentions that Snaith translates it as "worthless godlings," which
combines two of the theories.

It is obvious, as one goes through this chapter, that much of it reflects a delineation of the Ten
Commandments, although in a different order (cf. Exod. 20:4-6). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY.

The VERB "turn" (BDB 815, KB 937, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense, negated) implies a turning from and a turning to (cf. Deut. 31:18,20; Hos. 3:1). This terrible
spiritual reality is expressed in Jer. 2:13! See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 19:5-8

5"'Now when you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to the Lord, you shall offer
it so that you may be accepted. 6It shall be eaten the same day you offer it, and the next day; but what
remains until the third day shall be burned with fire. 7So if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an offense;
it will not be accepted. 8Everyone who eats it will bear his iniquity, for he has profaned the holy thing of the
Lord; and that person shall be cut off from his people.

19:5 "peace offerings" See full note at Leviticus 3 and 7:28-34.

▣ "so that you may be accepted" There is no VERB in the MT. The
NOUN (BDB 953) has three connotations.

- goodwill, favor

- acceptance ‒ see here and Exod. 28:38; Lev. 1:3; 22:19,29; 23:11

- will, desire, pleasure

Proper offering, proper animal, proper place, proper ritual were all required for the sacrifice to be accepted
(i.e., Lev. 22:19,20,21). It is difficult to know if "the acceptance" is of the "offering" or the "offerer," possibly both.

19:6 "but what remains until the third day shall be burned with fire" This is possibly because the fellowship
meal was meant to include other Israelis and Levites. Israelites did not eat much meat and certainly an individual could
not eat this much meat at one time, so they were encouraged to invite their covenant partners to share with them.

There may be some kind of hygienic purpose to this regulation.

19:7 "So if it is eaten at all" This is an intensified grammatical construction (i.e., an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and IMPERFECT VERB from the same root, also note Lev. 19:17 and 20).

19:8 "the holy thing" The difference between "the most holy" and "the holy," in referring to sacrifices, has
to do with where the blood was placed.

- if taken into the inner shrine it became "most holy" and could be eaten only by priests

- if put on the altar of sacrifice (i.e., peace offerings) it was "holy" but could be eaten by nonpriests, priests and their families

▣ "that person shall be cut off from his people" This obviously refers to some kind of separation from
the people of God. Some see it as excommunication, while others see it as a divine death. The context implies death.
See note at Lev. 7:20.

9"'Now when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap to the very corners of your field, nor shall

19:9 "you shall not reap" This was a provision for the poor and sojourner (cf. Lev. 23:22; Deut. 23:4-25; 24:19-22).
They were not to completely harvest their field crops or vineyards in order that the poor and needy might have access to
gather something to eat.

- cursing depreciates the "divine image" in all humans; this depreciation is "felt" by how others act toward the handicapped one

Israelites could disagree and confront one another ([1] personally, see Ben Sira 9:3; [2] in a lawsuit,

love and respect for God.

is mandatory as we see ourselves in an appropriate relationship to God and, therefore, to others (cf. Deut. 32:35; Rom. 12:19).

great commandment" (cf. Matt. 5:43; 19:19; 22:39; Mark 12:31; Luke 10:27; Rom. 13:9; Gal. 5:14; James 2:8).

Read the Bible for All Its Worth, pp. 165-169.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What does "be holy" mean in this context?

- What is the theological purpose of these various laws?

- Is there a distinction between worship and daily life in these guidelines?

- Why is Lev. 19:18 so significant?

- What was the "practical" outcome of these guidelines?

- How is Lev. 19:26 different from 19:31?
